consequences: No durable local checkout exists yet; a fresh clone (verified with --recurse-submodules) is the recovery path. The workspace model change needs a bitty-docs/umbrella AGENTS.md follow-up.
context: The workspace path $BITTY_WORKSPACE/bitty-plugins is a grouping directory holding four live plugin repositories with uncommitted changes and registered worktrees; initializing the new repository there would entangle active work.
decision_body: Create, gate, and push the new repository from /tmp/opencode/bitty-plugins; the durable workspace checkout is deferred until the grouping directory is retired.
title: Build and push from a /tmp checkout for the bootstrap

consequences: Metadata refresh is network-dependent and non-blocking; offline runs leave the index unchanged with a notice.
context: Registry entries must stay minimal and must not duplicate version/stars/dates; the store and future CLI must consume one artifact.
decision_body: scripts/sync-metadata.ts fetches bitty-plugin.toml (bounded, credential-free) and writes an optional metadata object into generated/registry.json; generate-index preserves it across regenerations and drops it for removed entries.
title: Derived manifest metadata lives only in generated/registry.json

consequences: Root devDependencies have no automated updates until the follow-up completes.
context: The bun ecosystem updater for this repository failed in its updater container on the first run.
decision_body: Ship dependabot.yml with github-actions updates only; track re-enabling bun in TODO.md. The npm updater stays excluded as known-broken.
title: Remove the Dependabot bun updater after a failed trial

consequences: Single source of truth; no duplicated JSON under app/; dev and build both require the committed artifact to exist.
context: The deployed store must fetch generated/registry.json as a static asset, and a second copy under app/public would drift from the committed artifact.
decision_body: app/vite.config.ts adds an inline bitty-registry plugin: it serves /registry.json from generated/registry.json in dev and emits it beside index.html as a bundle asset at build time; the build fails loudly when the file is missing.
title: Emit registry.json through a Vite plugin instead of committing a copy

consequences: No duplicate rendering or per-route build step; payloads are client-rendered and depend on Cloudflare applying the fallback only for non-asset paths.
context: Routes /plugins/<id>, /categories/<c>, and /authors/<a> are dynamic and the registry is fetched at runtime.
decision_body: Single Vite bundle with History API routing; app/public/_redirects declares /* /index.html 200 for Cloudflare Pages; documented in README.
title: Cloudflare Pages SPA fallback instead of per-route HTML

consequences: Fail-closed deployment with graceful degradation; a green run can still mean 'not deployed', which the summary states explicitly; re-run after provisioning.
context: plugins.bitty.run is newly registered; verification, the Pages project, and credentials may not exist yet, and pushes to main must not fail on unrelated work.
decision_body: deploy.yml preflight marks provisioned=false with a run-summary notice when CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN/CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID are absent; the deploy step is if-guarded, the build still runs, and nothing deploys with partial credentials.
title: Skip deploy with a notice when Cloudflare credentials are absent

consequences: Registry entries cannot express cross-plugin dependencies yet; deterministic rejection replaces a confusing unknown-key error; README/CHANGELOG document the decision and the future authorization path.
context: Research R9: plugin manifests may declare [dependencies], but the registry has no dependency field and ENTRY_KEYS rejects the table as a generic unknown key. Option (a) would add optional registry dependencies {id: range} with version intersection and cycle detection; option (b) declares dependencies unsupported at the registry layer with an explicit error.
decision_body: Chose (b). A registry entry declaring [dependencies] is rejected with an explicit 'not supported in registry entries' error. Plugin dependencies stay in bitty-plugin.toml [dependencies]. The manifest-side pairing (rejecting [dependencies] in SDK/plugin validators) is a cross-repo follow-up, out of this slice.
rationale: Phase-1 scope and bitty-plugins AGENTS.md forbid inventing manifest/registry semantics: a registry dependency graph (intersection + cycle detection + index field) is a new cross-repository contract that must be separately authorized. A safe, minimal, discoverable rejection prevents an installer from seeing an unresolvable dependency.
title: R9: registry dependencies unsupported in phase 1 (option b)

consequences: Validation now emits 5 warnings (one per official entry bitty range); zero entries or manifests break; generated index unchanged. Full convergence remains open and must land as a separate decision before 0.1.0. Adjacent item: resolver caret zero-major tightening vs SDK mock same-major caret for ^0.1 is a semantic divergence owned by SDK/docs, out of scope for the registry grammar.
context: Empirical CTX-0016 probe (scratch copy of bitty-package): resolver REJECTS partial comparator versions (>=0.5,<1.0; >=2.30; 0.1; >=0.5; <1.0), * and ||, caret+comma, leading zeros, >128 bytes; ACCEPTS ^0.1 (>=0.1.0 & <0.2.0), ~1.2.3, 1.2.3, 1.2.3+build, ^1, >=0.1.0. Registry accepts partial comparators, *, ||, caret+comma but rejects build metadata. SDK mock host accepts partial comparators and caret+comma, rejects * and ||, and its caret is same-major (^0.1 matches 0.9.9) unlike the resolver (^0.1 < 0.2.0). All 5 official entries use bitty = >=0.5,<1.0 or >=0.1,<1.0; all 5 plugin manifests plus the template and runtime fixture use the same partial ranges, and git-panel uses tools.git version >=2.30.
decision_body: Hard-reject in the registry now: wildcard *, disjunction ||, and ranges over 128 bytes (resolver and SDK both reject them, zero existing usages). Keep accepting partial comparator versions and caret/tilde-plus-comma, but emit a validation warning that names the range and reason (they are used by every entry and accepted by the SDK mock host; rejecting them would break the whole corpus). Keep rejecting build metadata (registry stricter than resolver, fail-closed). Do not converge further until the pending call chooses a side: extend resolver comparator grammar to accept shorthand, or rewrite entries/manifests to strict X.Y.Z.
title: CTX-0016: registry range grammar fail-closed tightening now, full resolver alignment deferred

consequences: README Dependency model section repaired (it previously promised rejecting [dependencies] in manifest validators); CHANGELOG updated; guard tests added in tests/registry.test.ts (registry rejection message points at the manifest; empty table rejected; manifest metadata path accepts [dependencies]). No behavior change in bitty-plugins tooling; registry entries continue to fail validation with the explicit DEC-0007 error.
context: DEC-0007 deferred a manifest-side pairing: reject [dependencies] in SDK and plugin validators because the registry has no dependency model. CTX-0015 investigated the accepted corpus before implementing that rejection. Accepted evidence: plugin-platform-rfc.md:153-154 defines the optional [dependencies] table (plugin ID to version range); :185-186 hard-limits it to 8 entries; :210 requires full-graph resolution before activation. package-followup-rfc.md (accepted):155-175 defines the closed constraint grammar with a 128-byte requirement budget; :227 the resolver graph budgets; :249-251 the prerelease opt-in flag in the manifest dependency entry. package-lifecycle-rfc.md:142 requires bounded dependency graphs in manifest validation; :167 binds dependency edges into H-B. Implementation evidence: bitty-plugin-sdk/src/manifest.ts:441-497 validates count/id/self-dependency/range; bitty/crates/bitty-plugin-host/src/manifest.rs:886-909 validates count/duplicates/range; all five official plugin repositories validate the table in scripts/validate-manifest.mjs. Rejecting [dependencies] in manifests would contradict the accepted manifest schema and every existing validator.
decision_body: Do not reject manifest [dependencies]. The registry-side DEC-0007 rejection stands because the registry entry schema has no dependency field. The asymmetry is deliberate: the manifest is the resolver input, the registry is a discovery index, and the accepted signed package index mirrors manifest dependency edges (package-followup-rfc.md:302). No SDK patch is required for the accepted string form. Fail-closed boundaries kept: table-form dependency entries (the undefined prerelease-flag syntax) stay rejected by the SDK and plugin validators until the owning corpus defines the syntax. Cross-repo defects found but not fixed here: bitty-runtime/src/plugin_runtime/manifest_toml.rs:163-168 rejects [dependencies] as an unsupported section although the accepted schema and the bitty-plugin-host model define it; the transitional validators in the plugin repositories still do charset-only range checks (R27 remainder). Follow-up requests: (1) bitty host runtime reader must accept [dependencies] per the accepted schema; (2) bitty-plugins-docs and the SDK must define the prerelease-flag entry syntax; (3) plugin repos may adopt the structural range parser.
rationale: Standing rule: fail closed where the accepted corpus is silent, and never change an accepted contract unilaterally. The corpus is not silent: manifest [dependencies] is accepted schema, so the DEC-0007 option-b manifest-side rejection must not be implemented; rejecting would break the accepted contract and existing plugin manifests. Registry-side rejection remains minimal and discoverable because the registry schema genuinely lacks the field.
title: Manifest [dependencies] is accepted corpus; do not reject it (registry-manifest asymmetry documented)
